normalized.governing_thought: Launch Copilot, but in a per-seat Pro tier, and after the mobile rewrite's next two quarters rather than as a $149 add-on in Q2
executive_summary: Recommendation: launch Dispatch Copilot inside a new Pro plan at $91 per seat (Core + $12) with a pooled AI allowance, targeting Q4 2027. Keep the mobile team intact through Q2 and use H1 to run a paid pilot on randomly chosen accounts.

The product works for engaged accounts: Beta accounts scheduled 11% more jobs per dispatcher-hour (matched accounts: +2%) and renewed at 97% vs 93%. All 240 were volunteers, so the gain is not yet proven for the wider base.
The prize is $1.2–2.9M of new ARR, not $8M: The 46% "likely to buy" came from the 6% of admins who replied, at larger accounts. When beta accounts were actually asked to pay $149 a month, 14% did.

Price per seat, inside Pro, with a usage pool: A flat $149 add-on attracts the heaviest users: buyers' AI cost is $61 a month. Pro at +$12/seat with 600 requests per seat matches Routewise and holds gross margin at 75% or more. Giving Copilot away in Core would cut margin to ~70%.

Protect mobile first: it is the bigger churn driver: Mobile reliability is the main reason for 27% of churn; AI for 6%. A two-quarter mobile delay loses an estimated $0.5–1.1M ARR for good. A two-quarter Copilot delay puts at most ~$0.6M at risk.
105% NRR needs both levers: Pro lifts NRR by 2.5–5.0 points once, as accounts migrate. Fixing mobile churn adds 1.9–3.8 points every year. Only the two together reach 105% in the low case.
Bring launch forward to Q2 if the CTO can staff Copilot without the mobile team, or if the Q4 2026 win rate against Routewise fell below 37% with no Routewise discount running.

slides.title: Choices made where the pack is silent, and what would change the answer

claims.claim: Choices we made
evidence: Low case = half the observed rate for both paid options (7% add-on, 16.5% Pro), because the evidence comes from volunteers or a different tier.

normalized.recommendation: Launch Dispatch Copilot inside a new Pro plan at $91 per seat (Core + $12) with a pooled AI allowance (600 AI requests per seat per month, extra packs at $20 per 1,000), targeting Q4 2027. Keep the mobile team intact through Q2 and use H1 to run a paid pilot on randomly chosen accounts (~500 + control). No standalone add-on, no Copilot in Core. Bring launch forward to Q2 if the CTO can staff Copilot without the mobile team, or if the Q4 2026 win rate against Routewise fell below 37% with no Routewise discount running.

Rejected: no new ARR, –$4.4M a year contribution, company gross margin 70.3% breaks the 75% floor, payback never; "Matches, but gives the value away".

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data; the briefing pack was the only input and no questions could be put to the requester.
Low case = half the observed rate for both paid options (7% add-on, 16.5% Pro), because the evidence comes from volunteers or a different tier.

Pool of 600 requests and packs at $20 per 1,000 are design proposals, to be tested in the pilot.
All 240 beta accounts volunteered; volunteering signals engagement that matching may not remove. Matching criteria not stated.
Beta accounts are not typical (8.1 seats vs 6.2) and usage is concentrated (top 10% made 58% of AI requests).
Hours saved are self-reported; renewal is measured over 90 days only.
Paywall test sample is small: 17 of 120 (14%); true rate plausibly 9–22%; 14% is a ceiling.
